executive_findings.finding: SBI Holdings disclosed that it invested in Ripple in 2016 and held approximately 9% of Ripple as its outside largest shareholder as of its June 9, 2025 announcement. The same announcement says SBI Holdings and SBI Shinsei Bank each invested $25M in Circle at its NYSE listing, $50M total.
executive_findings.implication: SBI is a disclosed strategic equity bridge to both Ripple and Circle. This establishes common-investor connectivity, not a direct Ripple-Circle partnership or coordinated control.

executive_findings.finding: SBI Holdings and Circle formed SBI Circle Holdings as a 50/50 joint venture to promote USDC in Japan and develop use cases. SBI VC Trade began retail USDC service in March 2025 after obtaining Japan's electronic payment instrument service registration.
executive_findings.implication: Circle's Japan strategy has equity, licensing/distribution, banking and product-integration layers, not merely a token listing.

executive_findings.finding: SBI Ripple Asia is a joint venture between SBI Holdings and Ripple. SBI's group-company page reports SBI Group voting rights of 60% as of March 31, 2026. SBI Remit, SBI VC Trade, Ripple and SBI Ripple Asia announced XRP-based remittance expansion to the Philippines, Vietnam and Indonesia in September 2023.
executive_findings.implication: The SBI-Ripple relationship has operational payment activity, not only equity ownership. Current corridor-level XRP volume and net flow are not disclosed in the captured sources.

executive_findings.finding: SBI Ripple Asia's February 26, 2026 conceptual proof of concept considered XRPL for tokenized deposits and deposit-based digital money using SBI's MoneyTap domestic transfer infrastructure and an SBI Ripple Asia token-issuance platform.
executive_findings.implication: This is an explicit XRPL institutional-finance design/PoC, not evidence that a production deposit token has been issued on XRPL or that JPYSC uses XRPL.

executive_findings.finding: SBI VC Trade and Ripple announced RLUSD availability in Japan on June 24, 2026 under SBI VC Trade's Japanese electronic-payment-instrument classification. The announcement describes free deposits and withdrawals. The captured official text does not specify the blockchain network.
executive_findings.implication: SBI VC Trade distributes both Circle's USDC and Ripple's RLUSD. This is a same-platform distribution channel and competitive as well as complementary stablecoin access.

executive_findings.finding: JPYSC is a separate yen-denominated trust-type stablecoin issued by SBI Shinsei Trust Bank, developed with Startale and distributed by SBI VC Trade. Its June 24, 2026 initial availability was limited to SBI VC Trade accounts; external wallet withdrawals were not enabled. Public-chain circulation was planned after legal and tax treatment was clarified.
executive_findings.implication: Do not assume JPYSC is an XRP Ledger asset, an RLUSD/USDC wrapper or a public-chain token at launch. The official announcement does not identify a public-chain deployment.

executive_findings.finding: On November 2, 2026 SBI VC Trade reported JPYSC handling balance above ¥30B and JPYSC Lending balance above ¥10B. The lending product is customers lending JPYSC to SBI VC Trade for a fee, not customers borrowing against JPYSC.
executive_findings.implication: The two balances must not be summed as new capital or interpreted as collateralized borrowing. Beneficial ownership and overlap between the measures are not disclosed.

executive_findings.finding: SBI and Startale joined the Open Standard in October 2026 and said they would consider an interoperability proof of concept between JPYSC and OUSD. The announcement lists Coinbase among more than 140 participating organizations.
executive_findings.implication: SBI/Startale and Coinbase have a shared consortium connection. This does not establish a bilateral Coinbase-SBI integration, a completed bridge or Circle's participation in that specific proposed test.

executive_findings.finding: SBI and Startale signed an MOU with BlackRock on October 27, 2026 concerning a digital-asset ecosystem linking a tokenized money-market fund and JPYSC. On October 30, SBI and SMBC announced a capital/operational alliance to study stablecoin use cases, with SMBC agreeing to take a 5% stake in SBI Startale Marketing.
executive_findings.implication: SBI's yen stablecoin strategy is expanding into tokenized fund and banking relationships. Neither announcement identifies XRPL as the settlement chain.

executive_findings.finding: Circle's September 17, 2026 Form 8-K discloses a five-year expanded USDC commercial arrangement with Binance: Circle pays a monthly incentive tied to USDC held through Circle's Modular Smart Contract Wallet infrastructure and Binance promotes USDC. Circle also sold Binance 1,237,011 Class A shares at $80.84 for $100M. Binance retained voting rights and accepted transfer/hedging restrictions generally lasting up to two years, subject to exceptions.
executive_findings.implication: Circle has a material equity and commercial relationship with Binance as well as relationships with Coinbase and SBI. The Binance investment is not evidence of XRP ownership or XRP-specific liquidity support.

executive_findings.finding: Coinbase's Q3 2026 SEC filing says its arrangement with Circle was renewed on the same terms. Coinbase reported Q3 stablecoin revenue of $306.905M versus $324.534M in Q3 2025, and Q3 USDC rewards expense of $129.245M versus $111.570M. Coinbase separately said average USDC held in its products reached $22B, about 30% of average USDC market capitalization, and that it captured approximately 50% of USDC economics over the prior year.
executive_findings.implication: Coinbase is a major USDC distribution/economics channel, but balance growth does not equal XRP purchases. The 50% figure is Coinbase's own aggregate characterization; its precise accounting definition and product-level net margin are not supplied in the cited earnings summary.

executive_findings.finding: Coinbase announced RLUSD availability on Coinbase Prime, Coinbase Exchange and the Coinbase app on October 28, 2026.
executive_findings.implication: Coinbase now distributes both USDC and RLUSD. This is a direct product listing, not proof of a Ripple-Coinbase equity partnership or universal RLUSD collateral eligibility.

executive_findings.finding: Three XRP derivatives aggregators reported materially different open-interest totals on November 2: TradRadar $1.93B at 12:45 UTC; Kodexius $808.65M at 22:19 UTC; Liqwall $1.39B at 23:52 UTC. Observation times, venue/contract coverage and aggregation methods differ.
executive_findings.implication: Aggregate OI is a conflicting, non-canonical feature. No average or stitched total is valid until raw contract identifiers, settlement assets, multipliers, conversion marks, timestamps and venue coverage are reconciled.

data_quality_controls: Keep company releases, SEC filings, independent journalism and third-party aggregators in separate source classes.
Official releases establish what a company announced, not independent proof of commercial success or price impact.
Do not treat SBI's Circle and Ripple equity interests as direct Circle-Ripple ownership or partnership.
Do not assume JPYSC is issued on XRPL; initial launch was account-restricted and official release did not identify a public-chain deployment.

Do not assume RLUSD on SBI VC Trade is supported on XRPL; official captured announcement did not specify network. A secondary report says initial Japanese listing was Ethereum-only; retain as secondary-reported.
Do not add JPYSC handling balance to JPYSC Lending balance; measures may overlap and have different meanings.
Do not treat customer JPYSC lending to SBI VC Trade as customers borrowing against JPYSC.
Do not infer XRP spot purchases from stablecoin issuance, balances, exchange reserves or corporate equity investments.
Do not infer XRP bridge usage from XRPL deployment or tokenization PoCs.
Do not average XRP OI providers or infer independence from brand names; capture raw venue-level inputs.
Do not treat Binance outflows, Circle freezes or XRP liquidations as direct XRP selling without transaction and venue-flow linkage.
